note: Defects in the decimal cores, written back into the code on purpose.
tools/mutate-decimal.sh applies each one to a copy of its host's tree and
Why: at 0.9.2 the C++ multiply rounded both operands to 18 fractional digits
whenever both had more, and every lane was green -- the only decimal oracle
then generated operands of at most 12 integer and 6 fractional digits, so no
product ever reached the broken path. An oracle only covers the inputs it
generates; a mutant that survives names the input it never generates.
Each entry: name (unique), host (js php python cpp lisp go rust), file
(relative to the repository root), from (must occur EXACTLY once in file:
a stale pattern is a suite error, never a pass), to, class (the bug class),
note (what the defect is). Optional: equivalent (a reason the mutant cannot
change any observable result; reported apart, and an error if it is caught).
